chunks: And by his chain, from Al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man asked my father (may the prayers of Allah be upon him) about the wars of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and the questioner was from our lovers, so Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him:

Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with five swords; three of them are brandished, so they will not be sheathed until war puts down its burdens, and war will not put down its burdens until the sun rises from its west. When the sun rises from its west, all people will be safe on that day, so on that day no soul's faith will benefit it if it had not believed before or acquired good through its faith. And one of them is restrained, and one of them is sheathed, which was unsheathed to other than us, and its ruling is for us.

As for the three brandished swords: one is against the Arab polytheists. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'So kill the polytheists wherever you find them...' If they repent (meaning they believe) and establish prayer and pay zakat, then they are your brothers in religion. So for these, nothing will be accepted except killing or entering Islam, and their wealth and offspring will be captives, according to what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) established, for he took captives, forgave, and accepted ransom.

The second sword is against the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Zimma). Allah the Exalted said: 'And speak to people good words.' This verse was revealed regarding the People of the Covenant, then it was abrogated by His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: 'Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day... from those who were given the Book, until they pay the jizyah with their own hands and they are humbled.'

So whoever of them is in the House of Islam, nothing will be accepted from them except the jizyah or killing, and their wealth is war booty and their offspring are captives. When they accept the jizyah upon themselves, taking them as captives is prohibited for us, their wealth is prohibited, and marrying them is permissible for us. And whoever of them is in the House of War, it is permissible for us to take them as captives and their wealth, and marrying them is not permissible for us, and nothing will be accepted from them except entering the House of Islam, or the jizyah, or killing.

The third sword is a sword against the non-Arab polytheists, meaning the Turks, the Daylam, and the Khazar. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said in the beginning of the chapter where He mentions those who disbelieved, after relating their story, then said: 'So strike the necks until, when you have overcome them, then bind (them) firmly, then either (grant) favor afterwards or ransom (until) war puts down its burdens.'

As for His saying: 'Then either (grant) favor afterwards,' meaning after taking captives from them, and 'or ransom,' meaning the ransoming between them and the people of Islam. So for these, nothing will be accepted except killing or entering Islam, and marrying them is not permissible for us as long as they are in the House of War.

As for the restrained sword, it is a sword against the people of rebellion and interpretation. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And if two parties of the believers quarrel, make reconciliation between them; but if one of them acts wrongfully towards the other, fight that which acts wrongfully until it returns to Allah's Command.' When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, among you is one who will fight after me upon interpretation, just as I fought upon revelation.'

So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was asked, 'Who is he?' He said: 'The repairer of the sandal,' meaning the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). Ammar ibn Yassir said: 'I fought with this flag with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) three times, and this is the fourth. By Allah, if they struck us until they reached the palm leaves of Hajjar, we would know that we are upon the truth and they are upon falsehood.'

And the conduct of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) towards them was like the conduct of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) towards the people of Mecca on the day of the Conquest of Mecca, for he did not take their offspring as captives, and he said: 'Whoever closes his door is safe, and whoever throws down his weapon is safe.'

And similarly, the Commander of the Faithful (may the prayers of Allah be upon him) said on the Day of Basra: He called out to them: 'Do not take their offspring as captives, nor finish off the injured, nor pursue a fleeing one, and whoever closes his door and throws down his weapon is safe.'

As for the sheathed sword, it is the sword by which retaliation is established. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Life for life, and an eye for an eye.' So its unsheathing is to the guardians of the killed one, and its ruling is for us.

These are the swords with which Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). So whoever denies them, or denies one of them, or something from their conduct and rulings, has disbelieved in what Allah revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.أَهْلُ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims under Muslim rule)
key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَغْيِ: People of Rebellion (rebels within the community)
key_terms.خَاصِفُ النَّعْلِ: The repairer of the sandal (title for Imam Ali (as))

ai.seo_question: What are the five categories of jihad (swords) in Shia jurisprudence and who do they target?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the five categories of jihad by detailing the specific legal rulings for Arab polytheists, People of the Book, non-Arab polytheists, rebels (Ahl al-Bagh), and retaliation (Qisas). It uniquely links the 'restrained sword' against rebels to Imam Ali (as), citing his merciful conduct at Basra as a continuation of the Prophet’s example, thereby establishing a key Shia precedent for civil conflict jurisprudence. The text concludes that denial of any of these swords or their associated practices constitutes disbelief, emphasizing their divine origin and comprehensive nature.
